title: Rebuilding in Philadelphia and the Newark injunction
summary: John Gibson books them at the Standard Theater in Philadelphia, but Nazarro's injunction blocks the Newark Orpheum at Christmas.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: colored theater that we played in in Philadelphia called the Standard Theater, the manager's name was John Gibson, colored man who owns the theater and he decided he would take us in because he knew we would act. See all of us had played there before, all four of us had played there before in an act. But I'm coming back this time with just Buck and I and he booked us. He charged us -- to borrow money now you had to pay 10% of whatever you borrowed. He couldn't advance on salary less than 10%. Okay. So I borrowed a few dollars to get these costumes and things I needed, sweaters and shoes and taps and plates and all. I got the music in New York, I got the music and everything.

We opened up, good success, I got to get another booking. So I booked in Newark. So in Newark he enjoined us in getting on the stage -- enjoined, do you understand me? Put out an injunction against us not appearing in his theater -- against us appearing in the theater. So we couldn't appear according to

this injunction. To enjoin us from working on the stage at the Orpheum Theater in Newark, New Jersey, which happened during Christmas-time. We were unable to do any shopping for Christmas or any food for Christmas or money for food for Christmas. We were in a terrible state for the first time --
Yeah. So my next move -- I can't get no job in New York, I can't get none in Newark, so I won't be able to get a job in the west. So let me get out of New York, okay?
